sub_strands.values: Peace: It is enhanced as learners share their findings and provide positive feedback.

outcomes.text: identify the subject matter of a poem
analyse ideas in the poem
reiterate the role of poetry in passing information

skills.name: Say what a poem is about and what it teaches
skills.mastery: Chooses the subject of a poem (what it is about), the message the poet wants to pass on, and the idea in a line, and does not choose a detail as the subject or an idea the poem does not hold, in 8 of 10 new items.

prerequisites.reason: This skill builds on it. Proposed, to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher.
Grade 6 English taught it first. Proposed, to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher.

leads_to.reason: Grade 8 English builds on this skill. Proposed, to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher.
Grade 8 English builds on this skill. Proposed, to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher.

misconceptions.error: Takes a detail for the subject of the poem.

example.question: What is the poem mainly about.

misconceptions.cause: Common error of Kenyan learners of English.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "a bird on a branch" next to the right answer in a new sentence and ask again.
misconceptions.help: The subject is what the whole poem is about.
misconceptions.feedback: The subject of a poem is what the whole poem is about, not one image in it.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks a poem has no message.

example.question: What message does the poet want to pass on.
example.correct_answer: we should look after our environment

misconceptions.cause: Common error of Kenyan learners of English.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "there is no message" next to the right answer in a new sentence and ask again.
misconceptions.help: Ask: what does the poet want us to think about.
misconceptions.feedback: A poem usually passes on a message or feeling, such as caring for the environment or the value of hard work.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

misconceptions.error: Reads a line word for word where it means more.

example.question: In a poem, "the sun smiled on the fields". What does it mean.
example.correct_answer: the sunshine was warm and kind

misconceptions.cause: Common error of Kenyan learners of English.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "the sun had a mouth" next to the right answer in a new sentence and ask again.
misconceptions.help: The poet pictures the sun as a person.
misconceptions.feedback: Poets give things human qualities and use words in new ways. The sun smiled means the sunshine was warm and kind.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

misconceptions.error: Brings in an idea that is not in the poem.

example.question: Which message does the poem teach.
example.wrong_answer: a message the poem does not hold

misconceptions.cause: Common error of Kenyan learners of English.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "a message the poem does not hold" next to the right answer in a new sentence and ask again.
misconceptions.help: Check the idea against the lines.
misconceptions.feedback: The message must be supported by the lines of the poem.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

sub_strands.sub_strand: Functional Writing: Notices and Posters (Theme 15: Tourist attraction sites - kenya)

outcomes.text: outline the format of presenting notices and posters
design notices and posters on current issues

skills.name: Know the format of a notice and a poster
skills.mastery: Names the parts of a notice (heading, what, when, where, who to see, the writer and the date) and of a poster (a big heading, a few words, a picture, the details), and finds the part that is missing, in 8 of 10 new items.

misconceptions.error: Leaves out the date or time of a notice.

example.question: This notice has a heading, the place and the writer. What is missing: "SPORTS DAY. At the school field. Games Master."

misconceptions.cause: Common error of Kenyan learners of English.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "a picture" next to the right answer in a new sentence and ask again.
misconceptions.help: A notice must say when.
misconceptions.feedback: A notice tells what, when and where, and who to see, with the writer's name and the date.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

misconceptions.error: Writes a poster in long paragraphs.

example.question: Which is best for a poster.
example.wrong_answer: a long paragraph with every detail
example.correct_answer: a big heading and a few short lines

misconceptions.cause: Common error of Kenyan learners of English.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "a long paragraph with every detail" next to the right answer in a new sentence and ask again.
misconceptions.help: A poster must be read at a glance.
misconceptions.feedback: A poster has a big heading, a few words, a picture and only the key details.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

misconceptions.error: Mixes up the features of a notice and a poster.

example.question: Which has a picture to catch the eye.

misconceptions.cause: Common error of Kenyan learners of English.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "a notice" next to the right answer in a new sentence and ask again.
misconceptions.help: A poster uses a picture.
misconceptions.feedback: A poster usually has a picture and big letters to attract people. A notice gives the details briefly in words.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher

misconceptions.error: Forgets who wrote the notice.

example.question: Who signs a school notice.
example.correct_answer: the person who wrote it, with the date

misconceptions.cause: Common error of Kenyan learners of English.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "nobody" next to the right answer in a new sentence and ask again.
misconceptions.help: A reader must know who to ask.
misconceptions.feedback: A notice ends with the name and title of the writer and the date.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher
